ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure gives the piecewise linear waveform of the signal x(t) with respect to time t. It can be seen that x(t) starts from t=0, x=0, and within 0<t<1 rises along a straight line to t=1, x=1, so the slope of this segment is +1 sec^{-1}. Subsequently the waveform also has descending, rising, platform and other segments, and ends at t=4. Reasoning: The impulse response of the matched filter is nonzero within 0 to 4 seconds, so take the matching time T=4. For a real signal, the matched filter response can be written as h(t)=x(4-t). When 3<t<4, 4-t falls within 0<4-t<1, exactly corresponding to the first rising ramp segment of x(t) in the figure, whose slope is x'(4-t)=+1 sec^{-1}. Due to time reversal, h'(t)=d[x(4-t)]/dt=-x'(4-t), so the slope of h(t) within 3<t<4 is -1 sec^{-1}.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: x(t) is zero before t=0, rises linearly from x=0 at t=0 to x=1 at t=1, then continues with other pieces until it ends at t=4. From the text, h(t) is the matched-filter impulse response and is nonzero only from 0 to 4 s, so take T=4. Use h(t)=x(4-t). For 3<t<4, the argument 4-t lies in 0<4-t<1, which is exactly the rising ramp of x(t) with slope +1 sec^-1. Because of time reversal, h'(t)=-x'(4-t)=-1 sec^-1.
